intervals.label: regular observations (documented to December 2017)
intervals.note: Start: regular source observations since September 2008. End: the Crab dataset of the 2019 HAGAR paper runs from October 2008 to December 2017 (arXiv:1902.01081); that is the end of the documented data, not of observations.
intervals.quote: Regular source observations are running since September 2008.

intervals.label: operation after 2017 (not documented)
intervals.note: No source fetched dates the end of HAGAR observations. A 2024 review describes the array in the present tense; the status is carried forward from that and not confirmed.
intervals.quote: The HAGAR telescopes (Singh, et al. 2019) are located in Hanle in the Himalayas at 4500 m above sea level, on the same site as the 21 m diameter Cherenkov imaging telescope MACE

name: HAGAR telescope array
notes: No Appendix A technology class fits a non-imaging wavefront-sampling Cherenkov array; `other` is used with the technique described in the sourced `technology` string (A24).

placements.note: HAGAR is described as being on the same site as MACE; no separate HAGAR coordinate is published in the sources fetched.
placements.quote: The HAGAR telescopes (Singh, et al. 2019) are located in Hanle in the Himalayas at 4500 m above sea level, on the same site as the 21 m diameter Cherenkov imaging telescope MACE

altitude.quote: set-up at Hanle, at 4270 m amsl

mirror_area.quote: The total reflector area of all seven telescopes is about 31 m2

telescope_count.quote: consists of an array of seven atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes located at the center and corners of a hexagon inscribed in a circle of 50 meter radius

summary.plain: Seven small telescopes laid out in a hexagon about 50 metres in radius, each made of seven round mirrors, that time the arrival of the Cherenkov light front from air showers.
summary.technical: Seven telescopes at the centre and corners of a hexagon inscribed in a circle of 50 m radius; each has seven parabolic glass mirrors of 0.9 m diameter with f/d = 1; total reflector area about 31 m2.

technology.quote: consists of an array of seven atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes located at the center and corners of a hexagon inscribed in a circle of 50 meter radius
technology.value: Wavefront-sampling array of seven non-imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes in a hexagon of 50 m radius.
